text:
incident-bot: ALERT — elevated 5xx and timeouts observed on streaming gateway (us-east-1). Affects paging endpoints (/v1/stream/paged and /v1/stream/live). Percent 5xx baseline -> 0.3%, current -> 6.2%. Auto-escalation to on-call.

maria: ack. I'm pulling logs for gateway and proxy tiers. Any reports of customer 1:1 timeouts?

jake_oncall: i'm on it, taking on-call. suspected window: 2719001000-2719004800 per metric spikes. creating triage room.

sophia_se: support has 3 incoming tickets complaining about streaming cutouts and truncated chunks when clients cancel mid-flight. They include trace ids. forwarding now.

kevin_sre: quick check — are we seeing backend model pods returning 502/504 or are these gateway errors?

maria: initial look — gateway logs show chunked encoding errors and upstream read timeouts. Some gateway instances show repeated `HTTP/1.1 502` with `upstream prematurely closed connection` in the logs.

joystick (ops-bot): automated runbook hint: try gateway hotfix (rolling restart) if errors concentrated on < 30% instances. Use `runbook/streaming-gateway` for steps.

jake_oncall: running light rolling restart on canary gateway pool now (command: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/gateway-canary -n prod --record`). Will watch errors for 5m.

sophia_se: support: please flag customers with highest request rate. We should consider temporary rate limits for paging to reduce load while we triage.

maria: past 60s logs excerpt:
```
2026-03-15T17:21:12Z gateway-7bf9 READ_TIMEOUT upstream read error: context canceled while reading chunked body, trace=abc123
2026-03-15T17:21:13Z gateway-3c11 502 upstream prematurely closed connection to client, backend=runtime-22
2026-03-15T17:21:14Z runtime-22 200 chunk flush ok seq=342 client_cancel=false
2026-03-15T17:21:14Z runtime-22 500 abort during infer step, oom? pid=1229
```
Not uniform — some 200s, some 500s, frequent client cancel race.

kevin_sre: that looks like backend instability under certain request burst shapes. Could be memory pressure when many long-lived KV caches are hot. Any recent model rollouts or quantization changes?

maria: no model rollouts in the last 24h. There was a config tweak in batching parameters pushed 2h ago to improve throughput: `batch_max_latency_ms` lowered from 40 -> 20. Rolling back to 40 to test.

jake_oncall: initiating immediate config rollback on a single runtime pool to see effect. Patch command: `kubectl apply -f runtime-config-rollback.yaml -n prod`.

sophia_se: support update: two larger customers experiencing truncated responses in streaming widgets; they've seen reconnect attempts from frontends ~3-5 times per minute. Customer impact = high for those tenants.

maria: mitigation plan (short term):
- roll back batching latency change on runtime pools (in flight)
- force gateway canary to route heavy streaming to dedicated streaming pool (less shared traffic)
- add 3s streaming heartbeat on proxy to detect client cancels and drain KV cache earlier
- if errors persist, enable temporary 429 throttle on paging endpoints for non-enterprise plans

kevin_sre: add telemetry: capture full request headers and client abort flags for a 15m window to correlate. I can flip sampling to 100% for paging routes.

jake_oncall: rollback applied to pool-a. monitoring logs and metrics. initial signal: 5xx rate on that pool dropped from 7.1% -> 3.0% after 90s.

sophia_se: good. notifying affected customers with templated message and ETA 30m while we watch. support_lead prepping escalation email.

support_lead: sent notice to top-3 affected customers (IDs attached). We offered priority mitigation and a dedicated contact.

maria: observed gateway instance-level memory spikes correlated with long-lived streaming sessions. snippet:
```
PID 1229 mem: 12.8GB -> 18.9GB within 60s under heavy KV cache growth
socket read errors increased at same time
```
Suggest limit per-session KV cache growth and enable periodic cache eviction.

kevin_sre: creating a temporary GC-friendly env: `INFER_KV_CACHE_MAX_ITEMS=500` and rolling to streaming pool only. Pushing as hotfix via helm.

jake_oncall: applied INFER_KV_CACHE_MAX_ITEMS=500 to streaming pool; gateway canary now routed to that pool. Watching p50/p95 latency and 5xx.

ops-bot: metric update: cluster-wide streaming 5xx: 6.2% -> 2.7% after rollbacks + KV cap. Client cancel rate also down 40%.

sophia_se: support: we'll keep customers updated. please gather logs and example trace IDs for postmortem.

maria: next steps for post-incident:
- collect full traces for 15m window (2719001100-2719005000)
- reproduce with load test simulating high prefix overlap and frequent client cancels
- instrument GC and heap growth per runtime binary version
- implement KV cache eviction threshold and per-session size guard upstream

kevin_sre: agree. also propose a small gateway change to surface 499 vs 502 more clearly to callers so we can differentiate client cancellations vs upstream failures in alerts.

jake_oncall: passing on-call to kevin for long-term fix. handoff note: rollback done, KV cap applied, canary healthy. Leaving page open for 30m for monitoring.

kevin_sre: taking over on-call. I'll coordinate the postmortem and timeline. If anything spikes again, @maria please escalate immediately.

sophia_se: thanks all — closing incident notification once we confirm 30m steady state. I'll keep support synced for customer comms. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident state changed to MONITORING by jake_oncall.

kevin_sre: filing initial incident ticket and tagging for product/reliability review. ticket: PROD-STREAM-2719. collect owners for next 48h follow-up.
